subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What term does Dickens use for each of the five chapters of A Christmas Carol?
questions.explain: Dickens calls the chapters 'staves', a musical term for the lines of a carol, reinforcing the book's song-like structure.

questions.q: In which year was A Christmas Carol first published?
questions.explain: Dickens published A Christmas Carol in December 1843.

questions.q: Who was Scrooge's former business partner?
questions.explain: Jacob Marley, dead seven years, returns as a chained ghost to warn Scrooge.

questions.q: What is the name of Bob Cratchit's sickly youngest son?
questions.explain: Tiny Tim is the frail, kind-hearted Cratchit child who says 'God bless us, every one!'

questions.q: Which spirit visits Scrooge first?
options: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
questions.explain: After Marley's warning, the Ghost of Christmas Past is the first of the three spirits to appear, in Stave Two.

questions.q: What is the name of Scrooge's cheerful nephew?
questions.explain: Fred, Scrooge's nephew, repeatedly invites him to Christmas dinner despite Scrooge's rudeness.

questions.q: What are the names of the two allegorical children revealed beneath the Ghost of Christmas Present's robe?
questions.explain: The children Ignorance and Want symbolise the neglect of the poor in Victorian society.

questions.q: What is the title of Stave One?
options: The First of the Three Spirits
questions.explain: Stave One is titled 'Marley's Ghost' and establishes Scrooge's miserliness before Marley's visitation.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the character Fezziwig?
options: To act as a generous employer who contrasts with Scrooge's meanness
To warn Scrooge of his coming death
questions.explain: Fezziwig's warm Christmas party shows a kind employer, highlighting how differently Scrooge treats Bob Cratchit.

questions.q: Scrooge's transformation from a cold miser into a generous man most clearly develops which central theme?
questions.explain: Scrooge's change shows that even a hardened sinner can be redeemed, the novella's central moral.

questions.q: When Scrooge mentions 'prisons' and 'workhouses', he is referring to Victorian institutions intended for whom?
questions.explain: Workhouses, established under the 1834 Poor Law, housed the destitute in harsh conditions Dickens criticised.

questions.q: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come never speaks. What effect does this silence mainly create?
options: A sense of dread and foreboding about the future
A feeling of warmth and comfort
Comic relief after the earlier spirits
Confusion about who the ghost is
questions.explain: The silent, shrouded phantom's refusal to speak makes the unknown future feel frightening and inescapable.

questions.q: Scrooge's wish to 'decrease the surplus population' echoes which real Victorian idea?
questions.explain: The phrase reflects Malthusian thinking that the poor were a burden, an attitude Dickens condemns through Scrooge.

questions.q: Why is it significant that Dickens structures the novella as five 'staves' rather than chapters?
options: It reinforces the idea that the whole book is a Christmas carol
It shows the story is a tragedy
It signals that the events are unreliable
It divides the plot by different narrators
questions.explain: A 'stave' is part of a song, so the structure supports the festive, carol-like tone promised by the title.

questions.q: Why does Belle end her engagement to the younger Scrooge?
options: He has come to love money more than her
She is forced to marry someone else
He moves away to another country
She discovers he is already married
questions.explain: Belle releases Scrooge because a 'golden idol', his greed for wealth, has replaced his love for her.

questions.q: Dickens's sympathetic portrayal of poverty drew on which personal experience?
options: His father's imprisonment for debt and his own child labour in a factory
His years serving as a Member of Parliament
His training as a doctor among the poor
His childhood in a wealthy country estate
questions.explain: As a boy Dickens worked in a blacking factory while his father was in a debtors' prison, shaping his concern for the poor.

questions.q: Marley's line 'I wear the chain I forged in life' most directly conveys which idea?
options: That a selfish, greedy life brings lasting consequences
That Christmas should be celebrated quietly
That poverty is a personal choice
questions.explain: Marley's self-made chain warns Scrooge that a life devoted to money is punished after death.

questions.q: A spirit is described as 'a jolly Giant', clothed in a simple green robe and carrying a glowing torch amid heaps of food. Which ghost is this?
options: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
questions.explain: The abundant food, green robe and torch identify the generous, festive Ghost of Christmas Present.

questions.q: In which stave does Scrooge observe the Cratchit family enjoying their modest Christmas dinner?
questions.explain: The Ghost of Christmas Present shows the Cratchits' dinner in Stave Three, revealing their warmth despite poverty.

questions.q: Scrooge's response 'Are there no prisons?... And the workhouses?' when asked to give to charity best illustrates which attitude Dickens criticises?
options: The belief that the poor should be left to harsh institutions rather than helped by charity
The belief that the rich should pay higher taxes
The belief that Christmas should be a religious festival only
The belief that children should be educated for free
questions.explain: Scrooge's cold reply mocks the Victorian view that prisons and workhouses excused the wealthy from personal charity.

specSource: AQA GCSE English Literature (8702) specification; A Christmas Carol
